history.why: Your brief left out what FIX.1 is for (a framework bug, not yours). This is it: OVERSEER FIX (not a failing test: the code passes today; this step changes it). Today the routed experts keep their packed fp4 weights on device and decode them to bf16 for every chunk (EXPERTS_IMPL=loop), about 4 ms per weight matrix per chunk: host-side-free but a per-chunk weight rebuild, against agent rule 5. Change: convert every routed expert's w1/w2/w3 to bfp8 ONCE, at load (bfp8 holds every fp4 value of this checkpoint exactly; measured), and delete the per-chunk decode. The scaled model has 24 routed experts per chip, the same as a galaxy_4x4 chip; they fit in bfp8 (check plan.yaml's memory numbers and say what they are now). With the weights already bfp8, run the experts through the routed-expert op the repo uses for bfp8 expert weights (ttnn/ttnn/bringup/INDEX.md, repo_map.md) rather than a per-expert loop, where it works; if it does not, say why in BREADCRUMBS.md and keep the loop on bfp8 weights. Keep the old path only as a value of the EXPERTS_IMPL setting (tt/settings.py), not the default. Measure the experts' device time per layer per chunk before and after (the plain profile of one block or a timed loop, minutes, not per-op mode) and put both numbers in BREADCRUMBS.md and the setting's description. The gate reruns both frozen experts component tests and both full-block swap tests (swa layer 0, swa_engram layer 1); all must pass. Update known_issues/repo_map entries that describe the per-chunk decode.

New evidence; read /localdev/dnijemcevic/bringup/device_floor_probes/REPORT.md first. The probe measured every stage on the device: the RMS stage is exact (sum of x^2 1e-6, rsqrt 5e-7): do NOT extend the rms_norm fork, leave the RMS stage as it is. The linear is already at its best settings (rel 6.4e-4 on the mixes, only 2e-5..3.5e-4 at the step output). Essentially all of the mixes' error (7.2e-4 of 7.4e-4; the -3.4e-4 bias; the 1-3 % comb column) comes from ttnn.experimental.deepseek_prefill.mhc_split_sinkhorn: it does its fp32 work on the FPU (SEL matmul, add_tiles, the RB / CB sum matmuls, mul_tiles) and its SFPU copies read without UnpackToDestFp32, each a TF32 truncation; the same Sinkhorn from fp32 SFPU ops measures 5e-8. Fix: fork the op (bringup-fork-op skill: ttnn/ttnn/bringup/, behind an option, default off) and make it fp32: UnpackToDestFp32 on every copy_tile input, SFPU fp32 binary ops instead of add_tiles / mul_tiles, exact SFPU sums instead of the RB / CB matmuls, the SEL matmul as data movement; keep it fast (today 0.08 ms; the stock 400-op chain is 1.91 ms and is not acceptable as the default). Measure the step against the floor and the kernel's time. Optional and free: feed the linear x as a bf16 tensor (same precision, 0.49 vs 0.87 ms). L0 attn_hc may stay ~3.3x its unusually low floor (the linear's in-tile truncation; no multi-pass): report it, the owner will waive it.

Wrong op to fork (owner). Do NOT fork ttnn.experimental.deepseek_prefill.mhc_split_sinkhorn: delete ttnn/ttnn/bringup/mhc_split_sinkhorn/ and revert its INDEX.md / bringup_nanobind.cpp registration. The bring-up fork mhc_pre_ttnn already has an fp32 SFPU Sinkhorn: ttnn.bringup.mhc_pre_xing (CHANGELOG 'mhc_pre_xing'; kernels/mhc_pre_xing_compute.cpp: coefficients and a plain-SFPI Sinkhorn lane-wise in fp32, accurate exp, Newton reciprocal / rsqrt; ~21 us per call on xing40's 4x2), the sibling of the mhc_pre_xing_pack you already use: it takes the all-reduced packed row (column 24 = sum x^2) and returns hc [.., T, 24] = [pre | post | comb]. Its math is Xing's, not DeepSeek's; compare it with the official kernel (/localdev/dnijemcevic/bringup/deepseek_v41_flash_d_p/hf/inference/kernel.py hc_split_sinkhorn_kernel): DeepSeek pre = sigmoid(m * scale0 + base) + eps (Xing: no + eps); DeepSeek comb: softmax over the row + eps, then column / (column sum + eps), then (iters - 1) x (row / (row sum + eps), column / (column sum + eps)) (Xing: clamp logits, exp(L - rowmax), then iters x (row, column)); no clamp in DeepSeek. Extend mhc_pre_xing behind options (default off: Xing's program unchanged, its tests and xing40 / glm53 cases still pass; bringup-fork-op skill) for the DeepSeek variant, and use it in tt/mhc.py in place of mhc_split_sinkhorn, with a setting in tt/settings.py (default the new fp32 path; the old mhc_split_sinkhorn path selectable for A/B). Measure: the Sinkhorn alone, the whole mixes step, per layer per chunk, before / after, both paths; the error vs the floor per step (golden inputs).
